note: Research behind the masthead drawings (20 Oct 2026). Each place was checked as open, local and iconic from dated sources; the brief is what the Figma drawing was generated from.

12th-main.name: 12th Main Road
12th-main.caption: 12th Main, HAL 2nd Stage
12th-main.why: This is Indiranagar's eating-out street. A residential layout road has become a nearly continuous strip of cafes, restaurants and pubs. A food blogger who has reviewed a run of its restaurants advises against walking in without a booking on weekend nights, and praises one place for keeping out the street's honking. It meets 100 Feet Road at one of the neighbourhood's busiest signal junctions.
12th-main.brief: Best view: looking west along 12th Main toward the 100 Feet Road signal. Near the junction, very large old shade trees with wide umbrella crowns and long level limbs arch over the road from both sides and almost close over it. They look like rain trees; check on site. A low concrete median splits the road, with cars parked nose to tail along it. On the eastern stretch, a line of green-and-yellow autorickshaws is parked along the median. Foreground: a scooter rider, a stray dog trotting across, and a few people standing on the corner pavement beside a small kiosk hung with strips of snack packets. At the junction there is a traffic signal on a pole and shopfronts with signboards. A March 2026 community photo also shows a small sloping tiled roof right beside the signal. Looking east, the two sides differ: on the south side a glass-fronted 4-storey block; on the north side a shopfront, then an older house behind a compound wall and iron gate, with a coconut palm. Utility poles carry bundles of cable. In February-March, pink trumpet trees (Tabebuia, probably T. rosea) at the junction and along the road flower pale pink while nearly leafless (community photos from late Feb and late Mar 2026). Optional period figure: a photo from 13 Jan 2009, titled 'Indiranagar 12th Main', shows a seller in a red cap and red T-shirt holding up magazines and a food guide to cars and motorbikes stopped at a signal under a big tree canopy. Shop boards stay blank.

indiranagar-metro-station.name: Indiranagar metro station (Purple Line)
indiranagar-metro-station.caption: Indiranagar metro station, CMH Road
indiranagar-metro-station.why: It opened on 20 October 2011 as one of Namma Metro's first six stations, and the first section of the city's metro to run was the one through Indiranagar. For most visitors it is the way into the neighbourhood. It sits just off the junction of the two main roads, 100 Feet Road and CMH Road.
indiranagar-metro-station.brief: An elevated station that straddles CMH Road about 150-200 m west of the 100 Feet Road junction. The station sits on pairs of ochre-yellow columns joined by cross-beams, so traffic and autos pass straight underneath on either side of a planted median. The viaduct curves in from 100 Feet Road with a pipe railing along its edge. Above, a long shed roof on curved steel trusses and blue-grey steel columns covers two side platforms. The trains are silver with a thin purple stripe; the platform makes a good inset or second drawing. At street level, a line of green-and-yellow autorickshaws waits under the viaduct, and close rows of scooters and motorbikes are parked in front of the shops. A large shade tree stands on the pavement, with 3-4 storey shop buildings behind carrying stacked signboards (draw them blank).

glens-bakehouse.name: Glen's Bakehouse
glens-bakehouse.caption: Glen's Bakehouse, 100 Feet Road
glens-bakehouse.why: This is the owner's own reference: a white converted house with a tiled porch and a wrought-iron arched gate on 100 Feet Road, next door to Toit. With 14,463 Google reviews it is one of the city's best-known bakeries, and EazyDiner (4 Aug 2026) calls it 'One of the most popular bakehouse chains in Bangalore'.
glens-bakehouse.brief: Viewpoint: straight on from the 100 Feet Road pavement, looking west. The concrete metro pillar (P63) can frame the left edge. A white two-storey converted house. Upper storey: a plain white block under a thin, flat, overhanging roof slab on visible rafters. At upper left, the GLEN'S BAKEHOUSE name sits in an ornate oval badge (draw the name only). At right, a small window with open wooden shutters under a little hood. A low terracotta-tiled lean-to porch roof runs across the ground floor. In the centre it is broken by a white rendered round arch holding an open, ornate white wrought-iron scroll gate. Through the arch you see an exposed-brick wall and warm hanging lamps. There is a wall lantern on each side of the arch. Low white walls topped with scrolling wrought-iron railings run along both sides. At left: potted conifers and a market umbrella. Right of the arch: a lit standing signboard (name only). In front: a stone-slab path, with scooters parked at right. Behind at left rises a tall Norfolk pine. Draw it at dusk with the porch lamps glowing, as in the owner's photo. Optional: Street View (Dec 2025) shows two later details, black line-art bakery murals on the upper walls with a red star on the corner, and a word ('JIREH') lettered on the arch crown. Both can be left out at small size.
sources: Owner's photo of the frontage (sent in chat, 20 Oct 2026)

toit.name: Toit Brewpub
toit.caption: Toit, 100 Feet Road
toit.why: Toit opened on 100 Feet Road in 2010 and is Bengaluru's best-known brewpub. Onmanorama says it 'gained iconic status among beer enthusiasts', and it has 62,775 Google reviews. Its steep wooden A-frame roof under the metro is instantly recognisable.
toit.brief: Viewpoint: a three-quarter view from the south-east, on the 100 Feet Road kerb. A fat fluted metro pillar and the underside of the elevated viaduct cross the top left. Left: Toit's signature steep A-frame roof, sloping almost to the ground. Its sloped faces are covered in a wooden trellis lattice, and a big round TOIT disc sign sits in the gable (name only). Below it, an open shopfront with green-framed glass doors and a counter. Right: a three-storey dark steel-and-glass block. It has a red exposed-brick panel on the first floor, AC units, a lattice-screened rooftop and a tall vertical green-wall panel on its edge. At street level: a bamboo-slat screen fence with a round sign, brick planters, dense palms that hide part of the front, bicycles, bollards and a waiting crowd. Draw it in the evening with warm lights.

chokkanathaswamy-temple.name: Shri Chokkanathaswamy Temple, Domlur
chokkanathaswamy-temple.caption: Chokkanathaswamy Temple, Domlur
chokkanathaswamy-temple.why: Inscriptions in Epigraphia Carnatica make this Domlur temple at least as old as 1200 CE, and Wikipedia's list of Chola temples, citing Deccan Herald, calls it the oldest temple in the city. It sits on Indiranagar's south-west edge, and Google even gives its address as 2nd Stage Indiranagar.
chokkanathaswamy-temple.brief: Based on Google Street View (Mar 2026) from the end of narrow Rama Temple Road, looking west at the east-facing front. The temple stands on a high stone plinth, reached by granite steps with steel handrails. On top is a flat-roofed entrance hall with square stone pillars and a deep cornice. Along its roofline runs a parapet of small painted stucco deity figures, rising in the centre to a small tiered tower with kalasha finials. A wide name board spans the entrance (blank or name only). The metal grille gates are decorated with the U-shaped Vaishnava namam mark. To the right, a compound wall painted in vertical red-and-white temple stripes (alternating stripes in ink). To the left, small shopfronts and houses. Behind: a tall coconut palm, a large leafy tree and newer apartment blocks. Scooters are parked at the foot of the steps, with a devotee or two. Soft early-morning light. Caution: a 2021 Wikimedia Commons front view shows the steps as twin flights meeting at a central landing, with a tall square stone lamp pillar on the platform. Check the 2026 Street View link before drawing the stair.

bobs-bar.name: Bob's Bar (Indiranagar flagship)
bobs-bar.caption: Bob's Bar, 100 Feet Road
bobs-bar.why: Time Out (7 Jan 2026) says 'Bob's is an institution' and that the 100 Feet Road original 'still has the most charm'. It is an old house under a huge rain tree, and it has about 21,000 Google reviews.
bobs-bar.brief: Based on Street View (Mar 2026), from the 100 Feet Road footpath looking west. At street level a long, low white compound wall curves gently inward between square white gateposts, each topped with a round globe lamp. The bar's name is painted on the wall in Kannada script (blank or name only), beside a small black stone house-name plaque (blank). Behind the wall is an older two-storey house, mostly hidden under a huge spreading rain tree whose trunk and canopy fill the upper right. On the first floor, a timber pergola frame holds a sagging canvas roof over terrace seating, with lanterns glowing underneath. To the left stands a taller neighbouring building with arched upper windows and a metal-grille gate. In front: concrete paving, a planter bed of shrubs and a young tree, a bicycle leaning on the wall, and scooters at the kerb. Draw it in the evening with the terrace lanterns lit.

notDrawn.someshwara-temple: INTACH calls this Chola-period temple 'one of the oldest temples in Bengaluru', and Wikipedia describes its towering eastern gopuram as typical 16th-century work. It is one metro stop west of Indiranagar in Halasuru, and its gopuram is the most striking silhouette near the neighbourhood.
notDrawn.rameshwaram-cafe: Marketing Monk says the now citywide South Indian chain began in 2021 from a 150 sq ft kiosk in Indiranagar. Its 100 Feet Road outlet, open till 1 am, is famous for fast-moving queues for ghee podi idli and has 21,485 Google reviews.
notDrawn.leela-palace: Open since 2001, this Mysore Palace-inspired hotel has domes, arches and nine acres of gardens. It is the grandest building on Indiranagar's southern edge (Kodihalli) and a citywide landmark.

reserves: Lavonne Cafe, Defence Colony: a respected pastry school and cafe since 2012, but the building is a modern box whose main feature is red neon script, which gets lost in one-colour ink. It would also be a second bakery next to Glen's.

Bhartiya Jalpan, 100 Feet Road at 13th Main: a long-running landmark, but it is only moderately iconic (3.6 on District, mixed reviews). Its drawing would rely on the shop lettering and a rain tree rather than the building.
